assumptions: The organism's usage table is the one named; CAI is relative to it.
limits: CAI needs a reference table; ENC and RCBS do not, which is why they are reported for any organism.
A bias measure is not a prediction of expression.
bio.jane/contract.question: How does this CDS's codon usage compare with an organism's: CAI, GC, rare codons, and the two reference-free bias measures?

description: Codon-usage analysis of an in-frame CDS: CAI / expression stats, GC, and every rare-codon occurrence for the chosen organism (pydna port), plus the two bias measures that need NO reference table — ENC (Wright 1990) and RCBS (Roymondal 2009), which are therefore computable for any organism.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

enc_bg_correction.description: correct ENC for the sequence's own base composition (Novembre 2002). Off is Wright's 1990 ENC, which reads GC-rich genes as more biased than they are.

enc_pairs.description: count codon PAIRS rather than single codons for ENC (k-mer 2) — bias in the junctions rather than in the codons.

feature.description: score this annotated CDS or gene by NAME instead of the selection (the panel's "A CDS / feature…" mode). Its own strand is used unless `reverse` says otherwise.

organism.description: reference organism for CAI weights + rare codons. Only some organisms carry CAI weights; the rest still get the rare-codon scan + GC.

rare_threshold.description: a codon is rare when its relative adaptiveness w = f/f_max falls below this. 0.30 is GenScript GenRCA's CFD cutoff, a convention rather than a measurement, so retune it per host. Only applies when table is set.

rcbs_directional.description: RCBS weights taken as max(observed/expected, expected/observed), so under-use counts as bias too rather than only over-use.

rcbs_mean.description: how the per-codon RCBS weights are averaged. Roymondal 2009 uses the geometric mean. Values: geometric (Geometric (Roymondal 2009)), arithmetic (Arithmetic).

reverse.description: read the region as the reverse complement. Leave unset to take the strand from the annotation when the selection is exactly an annotated CDS or gene, which is what the panel does.

table.description: score CAI and rare codons against a codon-usage table this project holds, BY NAME, as the Codon Usage panel lists it — any organism, not just the two pydna curates. Takes precedence over `organism`, and switches the rare-codon call from pydna's curated list to `rare_threshold`. Leave unset for the curated pydna report, which is the only arm carrying start/stop weights and the N-end half-life.

name: codon_usage_analysis

cai.description: Codon Adaptation Index, or null when nothing could be scored — check `caiAvailable` before comparing it, and `referenceTable` before comparing two runs

caiAvailable.description: whether a CAI could be computed at all. FALSE means `cai` is null because there was no reference to score against, NOT that adaptation is poor

codonMap.description: how often each of the 64 codons occurs in the measured region, laid out as the genetic-code chart: rows are the first two bases, columns the third

enc.description: effective number of codons, 20 (one per residue) to 61 (uniform) — needs no reference table

rareBasis.description: `curated` (pydna's published low-usage list for this organism — `rare_threshold` did not apply) or `threshold` (relative adaptiveness below `rare_threshold`). Rare counts from the two are different claims and do not compare

rareFraction.description: fraction of codons that are rare (0–1)

rareHits.description: every rare-codon occurrence with its position

rcbs.description: relative codon bias vs the sequence's own base composition; 0 = as predicted — needs no reference table

referenceTable.description: the project table CAI was scored against, or empty when the curated pydna organism answered

region.description: what was actually measured — the selection when there is one, otherwise the whole record, naming the STRAND and where it came from

strandSource.description: `explicit` (you passed `reverse`), `feature` (taken from the annotation the selection matches) or `default` (forwards, nothing said otherwise)
